title: Allu Arjun Called Ram Charan 'Mind-Blowing.' Nobody Expected It. Everybody Needed It.
excerpt: The Pushpa star became the first A-list Telugu actor to publicly endorse Peddi — and his pointed love for Janhvi Kapoor amid the objectification firestorm says everything.
body:
Two years of whispers. Two years of fan wars flooding every comment section from Hyderabad to Houston. Two years of "sources close to the family" confirming and then denying the rift. And then, on a quiet Monday night, **Allu Arjun** sat down, watched his cousin's film, and set fire to the entire rumor mill with seven words: *"Genuinely very proud of my brother."*

The post landed on X like a diplomatic treaty. Allu Arjun — the reigning king of Telugu box office, the man whose **Pushpa** franchise rewrote the commercial map of Indian cinema — had just publicly endorsed **Ram Charan**'s ***Peddi***. And in doing so, he became the first A-list Telugu superstar to break ranks and say what the industry had been whispering but nobody would say on the record: this film is special, and Charan is phenomenal in it.

> "Watched #Peddi last night. Mind-blowing performance by my dear @AlwaysRamCharan. A gritty, raw performance, extraordinary body transformation, and graceful dance moves. He absolutely aced it in every aspect." — Allu Arjun

https://x.com/alluarjun/status/2064219757998637524

The praise wasn't generic PR courtesy. It was specific, detailed, and dripping with genuine admiration — the kind you cannot fake. He called out Charan's body transformation (the actor trained for months to become a rural *pehalwan*, and every frame shows the work), his dance moves (still untouchable in Indian cinema), and the gritty intensity that Charan has been chasing since his **RRR** days. This is Bunny telling the world: my cousin just leveled up.

## The Mega-Allu Dynasty, Explained

For the uninitiated — and for the diaspora watching from New Jersey and Leicester and Brampton — the Mega and Allu families are Telugu cinema's equivalent of the Kennedys, except everyone looks like a movie star because they literally are. Ram Charan is the son of **Chiranjeevi**, the undisputed megastar of Telugu cinema. Allu Arjun is the son of producer **Allu Aravind** and Chiranjeevi's nephew. They grew up together. They built parallel box office kingdoms. And then, somewhere around 2024, the internet decided they were at war.

The rumors were never confirmed. But the silence between the two camps was deafening. At public events, they were cordial but never photographed laughing together. Fan armies waged daily wars on social media, treating every box office milestone as proof of one cousin's supremacy. Industry watchers at **Gulte** noted that Allu Arjun is "the first major Tollywood star hero to publicly shower praise on Peddi," adding that his post "grabbed the attention of both Mega and Allu fans." Both camps immediately claimed victory — which is perhaps the most Indian cinema thing imaginable.

## The Janhvi Kapoor Situation

But buried in the brotherly love was something sharper. Allu Arjun specifically wrote: *"Love to the leading lady, #JanhviKapoor."*

If you have been following *Peddi*'s first week, you know this is not just a polite shout-out. **Janhvi Kapoor** has been at the centre of a firestorm since the film's release. Audiences — particularly women's rights groups and a vocal section of social media — have slammed director **Buchi Babu Sana** for the way her character Achamma was shot on screen. The accusations are blunt: unnecessary objectification, uncomfortable camera angles, and romantic sequences that felt more like the male gaze unchecked than genuine storytelling.

The backlash was severe enough to force action. The director publicly acknowledged the misstep and confirmed several scenes have been trimmed from the theatrical print. "A few shots turned out misleading," Sana admitted. "We have taken corrective measures to remove them." Janhvi reportedly skipped the film's Hyderabad success meet. Veteran co-star **Jagapathi Babu** stepped up to defend her: *"Don't target her personally. She did what the director asked her to do. Sometimes it misfires. I support Janhvi Kapoor in this matter."*

**Jaya Bachchan** and **Kareena Kapoor** have also spoken out against the portrayal, widening the debate beyond Telugu cinema into a national conversation about female representation on screen.

And now, from entirely outside the film's team, Allu Arjun sending love to Janhvi by name. A small line in a long post. A very deliberate choice.

## Where Everyone Goes From Here

*Peddi* is sitting at ₹260+ crore worldwide and still climbing — Ram Charan's biggest solo hit by a distance, having smashed past $3 million in North America in just six days. The controversy has not dented the commercial run. If anything, it has made the film impossible to ignore.

As for the cousins: Allu Arjun is deep into **Raaka**, directed by **Atlee** (the man who made *Jawan* a ₹1,000-crore monster) and co-starring **Deepika Padukone**. Ram Charan is fielding multiple development deals. Both men are operating at the absolute peak of their commercial power, and for the first time in years, it looks like they are cheering for each other.

Director Buchi Babu Sana, responding to Allu Arjun's post, wrote: *"Your appreciation truly means a lot to me and to our entire team. Forever grateful for your encouragement, support, and blessings."*

And just like that, the loudest question in Telugu cinema — *are the cousins still speaking?* — has a very public, very warm answer.

They are. And they are watching each other's movies.
